supporting_observations.claim: The task was registered by dev.sharma under the expected \RB-IT\Deploy-VetChart name and runs msiexec against the VetChart 4.2 installer on the approved deployment share, matching the stated deployment practice and change calendar.
The task registration uses the same dev.sharma logon ID as a network logon recorded from WS-DSHARMA-01, consistent with the identified IT administrator performing the deployment.
The task is configured to trigger at registration time and run as dev.sharma with least privilege; the supplied records do not show an msiexec process or confirm that this task executed.

At 13:52, PROXY-RB-01 resolved WS-HITO-01 and then connected to it on TCP port 135; the workstation logged the inbound connection as handled by svchost.exe. The supplied records do not establish why the proxy host made this connection.

At 14:08, the workstation resolved mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com through the internal DNS server. This establishes a DNS lookup, not use of Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS or a connection to the resolved address.
services.exe set the Common Startup shell-folder registry value to the standard Startup directory. This record alone does not show that a startup item was created.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include the deployment ticket, the installer’s hash or signature, or evidence validating the installer’s contents.
The task registration record does not establish whether the task ran successfully; the supplied process records do not show msiexec execution attributable to it.
The records show the proxy host’s connection to TCP 135 but do not identify the initiating process or the purpose of that connection.
A DNS lookup for mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com does not establish subsequent network activity or use of an unapproved remote-access tool.
claims_not_established: Whether the scheduled deployment was authorized by the required ticket and whether the MSI on FILE-RB-01 was legitimate.
Whether the task executed, what changes it made, or whether it was later altered or removed.
Whether the inbound RPC connection from PROXY-RB-01 was authorized or part of malicious lateral movement.
Whether the Cloudflare-related DNS lookup led to a connection or use of an unapproved service.
Whether the Common Startup registry change was routine configuration or related to persistence.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify the deployment ticket and change approval; obtain the VetChart 4.2 MSI hash, signature, provenance, and file-access or installation records.
Collect Task Scheduler operational/history and task-file records, plus process and file telemetry around the scheduled trigger, to determine whether the task ran and what it did.
Investigate PROXY-RB-01 for the process, account, and purpose associated with its connection to WS-HITO-01 on TCP 135.
Correlate the DNS lookup with endpoint and proxy connection logs to determine whether any connection followed.
Inspect the Common Startup folder and related registry change context to determine whether any startup item was created.
